messages.subject: bad heuristic result?
messages.body_plain:
hi all,

i stumbled upon some odd behavior of heuristic(). i generate some fake 
data (following a model, i would like to test on real data, but am not 
sure, if the interactions i assume will be found) and learn a bayesian 
network with deal on this data. The heuristic method indeed finds a 
model very similar to the one used to generate the data, but with a 
peculiar set of parameters (i.e. the number of generated samples, 
standard deviations,...), the network returned by heuristic() clearly is 
_not_ the best one. i find this especially disturbing, as e.g. 
generating 1000 or 4000 samples instead of 2000 results in the "optimal" 
network being returned. has anyone else observed such behavior or might 
enlighten me as of why this happens? i need to know, if i can rely on 
this method before i get started with my more complex models...

thanks

markus


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 


library(deal)

nData<-2000
ngGroups<-20
ncGroups<-4

#generate the values of the two discrete variables
gGroup<-round(runif(nData,1,ngGroups),0)
cGroup<-round(runif(nData,1,ncGroups),0)

#generate means for all group combinations (used for TF)
muTF<-runif(ngGroups*ncGroups,1,5)
muTF<-matrix(muTF,ncol=ncGroups)

#generate TF values
TF<-numeric(nData)
for (i in 1:nData){
   TF[i]<-rnorm(1,muTF[gGroup[i],cGroup[i]],0.5)
}

#generate means for all gGroups (used for s)
muS<-runif(ngGroups,0,0.3)

#generate s values
s<-numeric(nData)
for(i in 1:nData){
   s[i]<-rnorm(1,muS[gGroup[i]],0.02)
}


#generate c
L<-runif(ncGroups,0,1)
c<-numeric(nData)
for (i in 1:nData)c[i]<-L[cGroup[i]]

#generate response values (including error)
response<-(rnorm(nData,0,1)+TF+c-s)

#BN-stuff
test<-data.frame(as.factor(gGroup),as.factor(cGroup),TF,s,response)
test.nw<-network(test)
test.prior<-jointprior(test.nw)
test.nw<-getnetwork(learn(test.nw,test,test.prior))
test.search<-autosearch(test.nw,test,test.prior,trace=T)
test.heuristic<-heuristic(getnetwork(test.search),test,test.prior,restart=3,degree=10,trace=TRUE,trylist=gettrylist(test.search)) 

test.bestNW<-getnetwork(test.heuristic)
plot(test.bestNW)

messages.subject: error with jointprior function
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Is there an upper limit on the number of variables deal is able to
cope with? I am attempting to use deal to construct a Bayesian network
to investigate whether relationships exist between gains and losses of
specific chromosomal regions. I have whole genome CGH data that
describes gain/loss of 813 distinct regions of the genome in 416
cases. I load this as a dataframe with
>P.27.7 <- read.delim(filename, header=T, row.names=1)
resulting in a dataframe with 813 rows and 416 columns.

Examining the structure of this object with str(P.27.7) returns
`data.frame':   416 obs. of  813 variables:
followed by a list of the 813 variables. The variables are all
factors. Theoretically there are 4 possible states for each variable
gain(G), loss(L), No change(NC) and amplification(AMP). However not
all varaibles have instances of all 4 states so some variables are
listed as factor with 4 states and some are factor with 3 states.

>P.27.7.inw <- network(P.27.7) #runs without error but then
> P.27.7.prior <- jointprior(P.27.7.inw)
returns
Error in array(1, Dim) : 'dim' specifies too large an array

Hence my question, is there an upper limit to the number of variables
that can be handled by deal?
For information purposes:
> traceback()
4: stop("'dim' specifies too large an array")
3: array(1, Dim)
2: jointdisc(nw, timetrace = timetrace)
1: jointprior(P.27.7.inw)

> sessionInfo()
R version 2.2.1, 2005-12-20, i686-redhat-linux-gnu

attached base packages:
[1] "tcltk"     "methods"   "stats"     "graphics"  "grDevices" "utils"   
[7] "datasets"  "base"    

other attached packages:
        deal dynamicGraph
    "1.2-27"    "0.2.0.2"

If any more debugging info is required please be specific what is
needed. I'm fairly new to R so I'm still learning how to debug but if
you tell me what functions you need the output from I'll post it.

best regards,
Richard

messages.subject: RE: error with jointprior function
messages.body_plain:
Hi Wei,

Thanks for your advice. Address limits and such things are well beyond my level of programming knowledge. At least it's stopped me wasting time on an impossible proposition. With regard to my purpose. My interest is in the progression of colorectal cancer through normal-adenoma-carcinoma-metastasis and the chromosome level changes that drive this progression. The dataset I described contains examples of all 4 stages, within this there are 59 particularly interesting cases where I have at least 3 of 4 stages from the same patient. 

At the moment I am investigating whether the different chromosomal changes that occur are really independent events or whether, for example, a change at site X increases the likelihood of a change at site Y. So I thought it might be interesting to see if I could use data to develop a network structure that described these relationships.To put it another way each of the 813 variables represents a region of the human genome, I would like to know if it is possible to predict the state of a given site(variable) if the states of some(all?) of the other sites(variables are known). Any thoughts on how to approach this?

You mentioned using BDe score if my variables are all categorical. They are so this might be a possible approach. I don't recognise the term BDe, could you recommend a reference(s). Is this something that is available in deal or should I be looking at one of the other R packages for Bayesian statistics.

If I make any progress I'll certainly keep you posted.
best regards,
Richard



-----Original Message-----
From: wei luo [mailto:weiluosfu at yahoo.com]
Sent: Fri 7/28/2006 19:55
To: Richard Birnie
Subject: RE: [dealsoftware] error with jointprior function
 
Hi Richard,

Sorry that my previous answer kind of misled you;
actually I believe that every computer program treats
4^813 ~ 64*10^486 as infinity. So it is hopeless to
compute a joint distribution of that many variables.

On the other hand, R does impose a limit on memory
usage: 
"There are also limits on individual objects.  On all
versions of R, the maximum length (number of elements)
of a vector is 2^31 - 1 ~ 2*10^9, as lengths are
stored as signed integers.  In addition, the storage
space cannot exceed the address limit, and if you try
to exceed that limit, the error message begins 'cannot
allocate vector of length'. The number of characters
in a character string is in theory only limited by the
address space."

I am not sure about your purpose, but you might be
interested in using the BDe score instead to learn a
Bayesian network, provided that all your variables are
discrete (categorical). With BDe, to specify priors
over parameters, you only need to specify an
equivalent sample size. As to structures, a uniform
prior is normally assumed.

Finally, if you are counting a sparse high-dimensional
table, a Hash-table often works quite well.

If possible, could you please keep me updated on
solutions you found or received?


Good luck,

Wei

messages.subject: RE: error with jointprior function
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Wei,

I'll look up that reference. I've just had a closer look at the original deal paper and it seems that BDe already is the criteria used for network scoring in deal. I'll have to read up how this works, I'm not a statistician so I'm learning as I go. In an earlier mail you suggested assuming a uniform prior rather than calculating it from the data. Since my problem seems to be the intractability of this calculation this seems a likely first step. If I can simply feed the deal learn function a vector of numbers intuitively this should be less demanding but I may be missing something. How do I actually calculate this in R? I assume I have to generate a vector of some kind containing the prior probability values but I'm a little confused. 

I have 813 variables each with 4 possible states so for a uniform prior the probability of any state for a given variable is 0.25 yes? So is the joint prior simply 0.25^813? That doesn't sound right, I think I'm missing something fundamental here. Any thoughts on what, Wei or anybody else?

regards,
Richard





-----Original Message-----
From: wei luo [mailto:weiluosfu at yahoo.com]
Sent: Mon 7/31/2006 07:23
To: Richard Birnie
Subject: RE: [dealsoftware] error with jointprior function
 
Hi Richard,

The application sounds very interesting. It would be
great if Bayesian networks turn out to be useful here.
 

BDe score is implemented in Weka,
http://www.cs.waikato.ac.nz/~remco/weka_bn/index.html

and BNT,
http://bnt.sourceforge.net/

I do not know any R implementation though.

The score of a network is actually the Bayesian
marginal likelihood when specific priors are taken for
parameters and it is described in:
    D. Heckerman, D. Geiger, D. M. Chickering.
Learning Bayesian networks: the combination of
knowledge and statistical data. Machine Learning,
20(3): 197-243, 1995.

Cheers,

Wei
